NVIDIA Vera: The Max Single-Threaded CPU at Scale. 

Agentic AI systems run sequentially, each reasoning step, tool call, and code execution happens one at a time on the CPU. When that CPU slows under load, the entire agentic loop slows and valuable GPUs go underutilized.

content: じゃけえさあ、「人間の意識は本物だから本物なんだ」って言っても別にトートロジーとは思わない。例えば数学の公理で「すべての自然数にはその次の数が存在する」に対して「それって本当なのか証明しろよ」とか言われても、公理は「そういう前提として話進めます」というだけの事で証明するしないとかじゃない。同様に「人間の意識が本物だって証明しろよ」とか言われても人間の意識は人間の意識だろ。人間の意識だってニセモノかもとか言い出す意味がまずわからん。人間の意識を意識って定義したわけ。人間の意識がニセモノだったら本物の意識って何だよマジで？それでだな、「LLMが意識のシミュレートあるいはモデルである」ってのはそこに哲学的議論の余地なくこれは実際的事実を言ってるまでの事なわけ。実際そうでしょ。もしも「いや、シミュレートでもモデルでもない！本当に人間と完全に同一の意識がそこにある！」とかいうならどういう意味で何を言ってるのか相当に説明を要しますな。LLMの意識なりが本当に人間と同じとは言えないって見りゃ分かると思うが。全然同じちゃうやん。本当に言いたいのは何らかの側面においてLLMと人間は似ているって話じゃないの？そうだとしたらそれこそがモデルって事だよ。本物の電車とプラレールは形はよく似てるけど大きさも材質も全然違う。特定の側面に限って似ている、それがモデルという事

画像生成ツールとして圧倒的な人気を誇るComfyUIですが、実は標準機能での「LoRA学習」にはいくつか深刻な技術的落とし穴があるようです！

・バケットモード（画像サイズを効率よく処理する機能）の不備によるメモリリーク
・Euler Samplerの同期バグ（ログ上の表示と実際の処理時間が大きくズレる現象）
・Kohya_ssなどの専門ツールに比べてメモリ管理が苦手で、すぐにメモリ不足（OOMエラー）になってしまう点

さらに、学習用の環境を無理に導入しようとすると、他の拡張機能が動かなくなる「依存関係の地獄」に陥るリスクもあります。

こうしたトラブルを避けるためにも、現在は「画像生成（推論）はComfyUIに特化させ、LoRA学習はKohya_ssやOneTrainerなどの専用ツールで行う」という分業体制が業界標準になっているようですね。

content:
【audio.cpp登場！Python不要で超高速なC++/GGML製オーディオAI基盤】
PythonやPyTorch、TensorFlowなどの重いライブラリへの依存から完全に脱却した、画期的な音声処理フレームワーク「audio.cpp」が素晴らしい進化を遂げています！✨

C++とGGML（GPU/CPU推論を高速化するライブラリ）だけでネイティブ実装されているため、推論速度が圧倒的で、システム全体もめちゃくちゃ軽量なんです。特定のモデルではリアルタイム性が5.15倍も向上した例もあるようで、音声処理が驚くほどサクサク動くのは感動的ですね！🚀

このフレームワークの凄さは、音声合成（TTS）だけでなく、音楽生成、効果音（SFX）作成、音声からボーカルや楽器音を分ける「ソース分離」、音声認識（ASR）まで、あらゆる音声タスクを1つでこなせちゃう点にあります。

さらに「パイプラインシステム」が優秀で、「音声をインプット ➡️ 音声区間検出（VAD）で分割 ➡️ 音声認識で文字起こし ➡️ 字幕ファイルを自動生成」といった複雑な連携処理をJSONファイル1つで実行可能です！

「mem_saver」モードという賢いメモリ節約機能も搭載されているため、実行後に不要なVRAM（ビデオメモリ）を適切に解放し、限られたGPU環境でも複数のモデルを安定して並列運用できるのが本当に実用的ですね。

音声AI開発やサーバー構築のハードルをグッと下げてくれる、今後の発展がとても楽しみなプロジェクトです！

LLM（大規模言語モデル）を自律的に動かす「AIエージェント」の開発において、避けて通れないのがデータの持たせ方ですよね。💡

実際に、JSONでは途中でデータが切り捨てられて失敗してしまったタスクでも、TOONを使うことで全てのデータを保持したまま見事に正解を導き出せたという実験結果も出ています！

さらに、データ構造の正しさをチェックする仕組み（バリデーション）も備わっており、データの信頼性もバッチリ確保。プライバシー重視の「ローカル環境（Local-first）」でコストを抑えつつ賢いAIエージェントを動かしたい時には、これ以上ない強力な武器になりそうですね。🚀

ComfyUIで話題の動画生成モデル「Wan 2.2 5B」を使っている時に、生成された動画が歪んでしまったり、全体的に怪しい紫色になってしまったりして困ったことはありませんか？実はこれ、設定を少し変えるだけでサクッと解決できちゃうんです！

👾 原因は「ノイズの削り具合」の競合にあり！
動画を生成する際、ノイズを除去する強度を決める「denoise（デノイズ）」という重要なパラメータがあります。これを「0.5」などの低い値に設定していると、元の画像の特徴を無理に残そうとする制約と、新しい動きを作ろうとするAIのノイズ調整がぶつかり合ってしまうんです。

心理コーチをしている受講生さんが、
本業の事務作業から、月に約22時間を取り戻しました。

会社員をやりながらコンテンツ販売にも挑戦している方です。

この人が置かれていた状況が、けっこう象徴的で。
職場のルール上、最新のAIツールは入れられない。
なのに事務作業は細かくて量が多くて、身体の負担まで感じていた。
「このままでは長く両立できない」と本人が言っていました。

そこで取った手が、地味に最強でした。
会社で使えるGeminiとGASだけを組み合わせて、自分専用の道具を4本、自作した。

【Before】毎月かならず出る決まった作業を、全部手で

・利用者情報の棚卸し　月5時間
・外注依頼シートの作成　1回30分（月4〜5回）
・利用者情報の検索と更新　1件15分（月40〜50件）
・非定型メールの振り分け　月8時間

【After】同じ作業を、ほぼワンクリックで

・利用者情報の棚卸し　15分
・外注依頼シートの作成　5分
・利用者情報の検索と更新　1件1分
・非定型メールの振り分け　20分

合計で、月に約1270分。約22時間です。
定常業務なので、年間にすると約264時間。

───────────

ここ、AIに詳しくない人向けに補足します。

やっているのは特別なことじゃなくて、
毎月かならず発生する決まった作業を、ほぼワンクリックで終わる形に変えただけ。
1件15分かけて手で探していたものが、1分で片づく。
その差が、40件50件と積み上がって、月22時間になります。

900名以上の事業者のAI講師を務めている僕から見て、
この成果がいいのは「時短」で止まっていないところです。

浮いた22時間を、コンテンツ事業を育てる時間に回している。
会社員のままだと踏み出しにくかった副業の土台を、時間で作っている。

AIは、時間の余裕がない人ほど効きます。

しかもこの人が使ったのは、最新のツールですらない。
環境が制限されていても「自分でも作れる」に変わった。
これは講座の受講生さんの基準値に囲まれたことが大きい、と本人も言っていました。

AIを「使う側」から「任せる側」に移すと、
売上より先に、まず時間が返ってきます。

Their ideas.
Their unfinished thoughts.
Their reading history.
Their obsessions.
Their patterns.

That changes everything.

It will be accumulated context.

Not because they’re smarter.

Because they stopped starting from zero every day.

Most vaults are storage systems.

content:
This is one of those projects that makes you stop and think...

"How the hell did nobody think of this before?"

Claude Code burns a ridiculous number of tokens on things you've already paid for:

• system prompts
• tool docs
• old chat history
• massive logs

pxpipe changes one thing.

It stops sending that bulky context as text.

Instead, it renders it into dense images that Claude can still read.

The result?

Up to ~70% lower Claude Code costs.

No prompt engineering.

No model switching.

No context summarization.

Just changing how the context is represented.

The insight is ridiculously clever:

> Text tokens scale with content.

> Image tokens scale with image size.

So if you can pack tens of thousands of characters into a single image that Claude reads reliably...

...you've just created a compression layer for LLMs.

That's the kind of idea that creates entirely new categories.

It's not perfect.

Exact identifiers, hashes, and secrets should still stay as text.

But for system prompts, documentation, tool outputs, and long histories?

This is an incredibly elegant hack.

I have a feeling we'll look back at this as one of the first projects that made people realize:

The next optimization isn't better prompts.

It's changing the medium the model reads.

pxpipe is one of the most creative AI infrastructure projects I've seen this year.

content:
🚨Three engineers—at Google, Anthropic, and OpenClaw—independently arrived at the same idea in the same week.

Now it has a name:

Loop Engineering.

The shift is deceptively simple:

Stop prompting your AI. Build the system that prompts it.

You're no longer inside the loop.

You're designing the loop.

Every cycle follows five steps:

→ Discovery — The agent finds work on its own (failing CI, open issues, stale PRs)

→ Handoff — Every task gets its own isolated git worktree so multiple agents never collide

→ Verification — A second agent assumes the first is wrong and reviews everything. The generator and the judge are never the same run

→ Persistence — Results are written to disk instead of disappearing with the context window

→ Scheduling — A timer wakes the system up again. That's what turns it into a continuous loop

The idea that completely changes how you think about AI agents:

> An AI reviewing its own work will almost always approve itself.

The solution isn't a smarter prompt.

It's a skeptical reviewer that exists outside the generation process.

This is already happening in production.

One Stripe engineering pipeline reportedly merges 1,300+ AI-generated pull requests every week.

Prompt engineering taught us how to talk to AI.

Loop engineering teaches AI how to keep working without us.

The original guide is just 11 pages.

If you're building with Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, or any coding agent, this is one of the most important reads of the year.

title: In a Patent Dispute, Where You Fight Often Matters Most | IPWatchdog Unleashed
content: In any patent dispute, the strength of the patent still matters. But increasingly, it is not the only thing that matters—or even, in some cases, the thing that matters most. That means where a patent dispute takes place cannot be a tactical afterthought or viewed as a choice of federal district courts in the United States alone. This is true today more than ever because despite patents ostensibly being property—at least according to the Patent Act—which tribunal and which judges make the ultimate decisions affecting the patent often matter most of all because patents and patent enforcement have become driven by ideology and the type of fervor normally reserved highly emotionally charged discussions, like religion and politics. title: UN experts warn Belarus political prisoners face continuing repression due to passport invalidation
content: UN experts on Monday warned that the expulsion of political prisoners from Belarus and subsequent invalidation of their passports may amount to transnational repression, increased statelessness, and human rights violations. Their concerns stem from the December 2025 release of 123 prisoners to Ukraine and Lithuania following negotiations with the United States. Most of these individuals were detained for peacefully exercising their rights. Among those released are activists within the Belarusian rights group Viasna , primary political opposition figures, and an editor of the largest news outlet in Belarus. Upon removal to Lithuania and Ukraine, eight prisoners discovered that their Belarusian passports were declared invalid without any notice or explanation, despite remaining valid at the time of their forcible expulsion. The experts stated that the arbitrary invalidation of documents severely affects these individuals’ essential rights, such as freedom of movement, legal status, family life, and access to employment, healthcare, and banking services. The December release was not the first or last group of political prisoners to be released in Belarus with no protections in place to safeguard their basic human rights. 250 arbitrarily detained individuals were released in March of this year, 52 were released in September 2025, and several were released in 2023, including Leanid Sudalenka, the former head of Human Rights Centre Viasna. In their report UN experts expressed their concerns over Sudalenka, who left Belarus due to continuing persecution and is now facing additional criminal investigations in absentia under their “special proceedings” framework for “extremist” offenses related to human rights activities and public expression. title: Hamas announces dissolution of Gaza governance
content: Leaders of the militant Palestinian group Hamas announced on Monday that it will dissolve its leadership in Gaza, engaging with the terms of the US-brokered peace deal and welcoming a technocratic governing committee. Hamas has governed the Gaza Strip for nearly two decades. Dr. Ismail al-Thawabta, the director general of the Government Media Office in Gaza, announced at a press conference that Hamas is dissolving its Government Emergency Committee. He called on “all concerned and competent parties to expedite the immediate steps” for the “National Committee of the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to exercise its duties and responsibilities” on behalf of the Palestinian people. According to Drop Site News, whose journalists spoke with officials at the announcement, Dr. al-Thawabta assured that there “would be no obstacles from Gaza’s civil service” and called on Israel to “withdraw its forces, stop the genocide and starvation, open the crossings, and let the NCAG in.” However, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar expressed doubt about the genuineness of the announcement and dismissed the statement. He stated on X that the announcement was a “trick.” The foreign minister added that Hamas is attempting to “prevent its own disarmament” and seeks to replicate the Iranian paramilitary wing Hezbollah. He called for the “complete demilitarization of the Gaza Strip.” The US-brokered peace plan, implemented by President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace , includes 20 comprehensive terms for both Israel and Hamas. Among these are terms to “demilitarize” Gaza “under the supervision of independent monitors.” The general commissioner of the NCAG, Dr. Ali Shaath, welcomed the announcement in a statement on X. He said the NCAG “stands fully prepared to assume its national responsibilities.” July 2, 2026, marked 1000 days of the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza. Gaza

title: UK financial regulator publishes landmark AI review
content: The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published a landmark review on Monday that proposes recommendations to regulate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the financial decisions made by consumers. The review, titled the Mills Review , anticipates that both consumers and firms will start delegating “more financial decision-making to AI systems,” including for agreements, initiating transactions, and executing decisions “within agreed parameters.” One of the key findings of the review outlined that while AI can help bridge advice gaps and “support growth,” there remain risks “associated with fraud, cyber security, and consumer harm.” Conducting the review, Sheldon Mills highlighted that “AI can also amplify risks: bias, discrimination, exclusion, opaque decision-making (particularly when multiple AI models interact), misleading or hallucinatory advice and erosion of consumer trust.” The review stated that presently, one in five adults in the UK are “already open to AI making decisions for them,” particularly when decisions feel “complex or high stakes.” It found that roughly 26 percent of the population “trust general-purpose tools such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini for financial advice” with little awareness that such platforms provide no “formal routes to recourse” or protections. Overall, the Mills Review identified four areas that it anticipates will be impacted by AI in the financial sector: “the transformation of firms,” “new consumer journeys,” “a reshaped competition landscape,” and “amplified financial crime and cyber risk.” The FCA projected the shift in how consumers and firms consult AI to take place by 2030. title: Illinois governor enacts legislation holding AI companies accountable for safety risks
content: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker on Monday signed into law a landmark artificial intelligence (AI) bill, cementing the state as a “national leader in setting guardrails for responsible innovation and growth.” Senate Bill 315 , or the AI Safety Measures Act, implements new safety regulations on AI companies developing frontier models , the most advanced and costliest AI models such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The act requires these companies to publish transparency frameworks that explain the company’s compliance with industry safety standards, the capabilities of the software and its potential to create “catastrophic risk,” and the company’s response to possible safety incidents any time that they deploy a new or substantially modified frontier model. Most notably, the law mandates that these companies undergo annual audits of safety issues by independent third parties and for the results to be published. This requirement is the first of its kind to be implemented into any state mandated AI legislation. The act also allows for the Illinois attorney general to impose civil penalties on companies that violate its provisions in the form of monetary fines of up to $1 million for the first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations, as well as lays out protections for whistleblowers and internal reporting schemes. At a press conference on Monday, Pritzker emphasized that these regulations were not made to hinder the growth of AI, only to create more transparency for users, stating: At the dawn of this technological revolution we face a choice. We can work together to establish thoughtful guardrails in ways that benefit both industry and the public, or we can allow a handful of actors to evade accountability and push the costs and detriments onto ordinary people. title: Automated Moderation Is Here to Stay
content: This blog post is part 1 of a 2-part series. The second part will set out recommendations for companies and policymakers. Six years ago—one month into a global pandemic—we argued that the automated moderation processes many platforms were rapidly adopting should be highly transparent, easily appealable, and temporary. We warned that "protocols adopted in times of crisis often persist when the crisis is over." That warning proved prescient. The use of automation and artificial intelligence (AI) to identify, flag, and moderate content has become the new norm—a permanent feature of how platforms govern speech online. In this two part series, we’re take stock of this new norm, and considering what platforms can and should do to ensure that AI serves online expression rather than stifling it. A brief history of automated content moderation From spam filtering and keyword blacklists to the hash-matching technologies used to identify child sexual abuse material and terrorist content, automated technologies have been used in commercial content moderation for many years. While these tools have long posed risks to freedom of expression, their use was, for quite some time, relatively limited in scope. Then, in 2017, a blog post published by Facebook (now Meta) described the company's "fairly recent" use of artificial intelligence to identify, classify, and remove violent extremist content. At the same time, Facebook emphasized caution, noting that it did not want to suggest there was "any easy technical fix." Just one year later, Mark Zuckerberg appeared before the U.S. Senate's Commerce and Judiciary Committees and disclosed that "99 percent of the ISIS and Al Qaida content" removed by Facebook was flagged by AI "before any human sees it." He also stated that Facebook was "developing A.I. tools that can identify certain classes of bad activity proactively and flag it for our team at Facebook."
